'''Georg von Freymann''' is a German experimental physicist and professor of [[physics]] at the [[Technical University of Kaiserslautern]] and head of the "Optical Technologies and Photonics" research group there.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physik.uni-kl.de/en/freymann|title=AG Optical Technologies and Photonics - TU Kaiserslautern|website=www.physik.uni-kl.de}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Georg von Freymann studied [[physics]] at the [[University of Karlsruhe]] from 1992 to 1998 and received his Ph.D. there in 2001 on the energy level statistics of excitons in semiconductors. During postdoctoral stays at the [[University of Karlsruhe|Research Center Karlsruhe]] and the [[University of Toronto]] (there in the groups of Sajeev John and Geoffrey A. Ozin), von Freymann focused on the field of three-dimensional [[photonic crystal]]s.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/person/1793837?language=en|title=DFG - GEPRIS - Professor Dr. Georg von Freymann|website=gepris.dfg.de}}</ref> As head of a DFG [[Emmy Noether Program|Emmy Noether junior research group]]<ref name="auto"/> at the Institute of Nanotechnology of the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT)]], von Freymann worked from 2005 to 2010 in particular on the fabrication of three-dimensional photonic nanostructures. In 2009, he followed the call as a substitute professor for applied physics at KIT and moved to the [[Technical University of Kaiserslautern]] as a professor in 2010.

From 2007 to 2014, von Freymann was [[Technical director|Technical Director]] of [[Nanoscribe]] GmbH, a company he co-founded in 2007. Among others, this company was awarded the DPG Technology Transfer Award in 2018.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/dpg-technologietransferpreis/preistraeger|title=Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger|website=DPG}}</ref> In addition to his work at the university, von Freymann was a group leader from 2011 to 2014 at the Fraunhofer Institute for Physical Measurement Techniques in Freiburg and has been a department head since 2013. His department for materials characterization and testing was incorporated into the Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.itwm.fraunhofer.de/en/departments/mc.html|title=Materials Characterization and Testing - Fraunhofer ITWM|website=Fraunhofer Institute for Industrial Mathematics ITWM}}</ref> in Kaiserslautern in 2017. He co-founded Opti-Cal GmbH in 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.opti-cal.de/english/company/|title=Shareholder|website=opti-cals Webseite!}}</ref> and is head of the Nanostructuring Center at the Technical University of Kaiserslautern since 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsc.uni-kl.de/en/staff|title=Staff - TU Kaiserslautern|website=www.nsc.uni-kl.de}}</ref> Von Freymann is a member of the Collaborative Research Centers SFB 926 "Component Surfaces", the SFB/Transregio 173 "Spin+X: Spin in its collective environment", the SFB/Transregio 185 "Open system control of atomic and photonic matter" of the [[German Research Foundation]], and the State Research Center for Optics and Material Sciences at the Technical University of Kaiserslautern<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://optimas.uni-kl.de/en/organization/members|title=Members - TU Kaiserslautern|website=optimas.uni-kl.de}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* 2003-2005: DFG research fellowship, stay at the [[University of Toronto]], Toronto, Canada<ref name="auto"/>
* 2005-2010: [[Emmy Noether Program|Emmy Noether Junior Research Group, DFG]]<ref name="auto"/>
* 2014: SPIE PRISM Award for 3D Printing (Nanoscribe GmbH)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spie.org/news/spie-professional-magazine-archive/2014-april/2014-prism-awards|title=2014 Prism Awards|website=spie.org}}</ref>
* Seit 2014: Vice speaker of the research building "Laboratory of Advanced Spin Engineering (LASE)", TU Kaiserslautern (new research building according to Art. 91b GG)
* 2018: [[German Physical Society|DPG]] Technology Transfer Award (Nanoscribe GmbH)<ref name="auto1"/>
* 2018: 1st prize at the [[Baden-Württemberg]] state award for young companies (Nanoscribe GmbH)<ref>https://www.kit.edu/kit/english/pi_2018_142_nanoscribe-wins-1st-prize-at-the-baden-wurttemberg-state-awards-for-young-companies.php Baden-Württemberg state award for young companies</ref>
* 2020: Innovation award of the state of [[Rhineland-Palatinate]] for 3D printing (Opti-Cal GmbH)<ref>https://innovationspreis.rlp.de/de/innovationspreis-2011-2021/innovationspreis-2020/ Innovation Award of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate 2020</ref>

== Research ==
Georg von Freymann's research spans from basic principles to industrial applications. The focus is on the technology of three-dimensional microprinting, which is mainly used for applications in [[photonics]] ranging from optical quantum simulators and bio-inspired photonic structures to calibration standards for areal optical metrology. His work also focuses on terahertz technology, ranging from [[terahertz radiation|terahertz wave]] generation and detection to industrial applications in nondestructive testing. The recently established terahertz quantum sensing technology opens up a completely new approach to terahertz metrology, since it eliminates the need for direct detection of the terahertz waves by suitably entangling the [[photon]]s and transfers the information into the [[electromagnetic spectrum|visible spectral range]].

== Publications ==
Georg von Freymann has published more than 190 papers in peer-reviewed international journals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://publons.com/researcher/2806813/georg-von-freymann/|title=Georg von Freymann's Publons profile|website=publons.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.de/citations?user=Tnm30dUAAAAJ&hl=de|title=Georg von Freymann|website=scholar.google.de}}</ref>
